requirements.instruction: Initialize the hierarchical evaluation run.
constraints: Set B to 0.
Set terminal_round to false.
The initial corpus becomes current round context.
Runtime behavior uses supplied configuration.

requirements.instruction: Evaluate the current B value and resolve the complete configurable iterator behavior for the current round.
constraints: Evaluate B at the beginning of every B round.
Apply the configured B rule matching the current B value.
The matching B rule may set or reference every setting defined as configurable on the iterator.
Resolve B before division or any other round-dependent operation.
The resolved iterator configuration applies for that B round.

requirements.instruction: Divide the current round context and assign bounded context to an ordered sequence of b batches.
constraints: divider.max_tokens is the maximum number of context tokens assignable to one b.
Call the single runtime token-counting function when testing a proposed b assignment.
Check the max_tokens condition exactly once when context is assigned to a newly created b.
Every assigned b context must be <= divider.max_tokens.
If a preferred division is oversized, shift division boundaries until all resulting assignments fit.
Once assigned, the b context remains established for the lifetime of that b, including retries.
The divider emits an ordered batch sequence.

requirements.instruction: Initialize the inner batch iterator for the current B round.
constraints: Set b to 0.
b identifies the current batch in the ordered batch sequence.

requirements.instruction: Assemble a fresh evaluator invocation for the current b.
constraints: Use the context already assigned to b.
Use the evaluator configuration resolved for this B round.
Evaluator configuration contains task, evaluation criteria, and response contract.
Task, criteria, response contract, prior responses, errors, and other invocation material are outside divider.max_tokens.
Do not recheck assigned context size during invocation assembly.
Every invocation is fresh and receives only explicitly assembled inputs.

requirements.instruction: Invoke the evaluator through the supplied Gemini API interface and capture the response and mechanically observable invocation state.
constraints: Record evaluator response and invocation success/failure.
Record mechanically observable information needed by later algorithm steps.

requirements.instruction: Evaluate configured retry conditionals when an evaluator invocation produces a condition covered by retry configuration.
constraints: Retry conditionals and retry attempts execute sequentially in configured order.
Each retry is a fresh evaluator invocation.
Each retry receives the runtime-supported inputs named by its conditional.
Retries may reuse the already assigned b context without another max_tokens assignment check.
The first retry that satisfies its configured success condition is retained and all later attempts are skipped.
Retry sequences are finite.
If all applicable retries fail, use the configured terminal retry result.

requirements.instruction: Parse and mechanically normalize an evaluator response according to its configured response contract.
constraints: Required fields come from the configured response contract.
Configured deterministic recovery may extract required fields from malformed serialization.
If required fields are mechanically recoverable, normalize without another model invocation.
Recovery strategies may be attempted in configured order.

requirements.instruction: Apply configured mechanical acceptance conditions to the evaluator response.
constraints: Acceptance conditions inspect mechanically observable properties only.
Conditions may include invocation status, required-field recovery, response token count, and other exposed mechanical values.
When response token count is required, call the single runtime token-counting function.
Response token thresholds are configured as divisors or ratios of divider.max_tokens.
The intended initial hard response threshold is divider.max_tokens / 2.
Response checks never remeasure assigned b context.
Acceptance results may lead to a configured retry conditional or a terminal b result.

requirements.instruction: Commit the terminal result and supervisory status of the current b.
constraints: Each b reaches success or failure before b advances.
Successful b retains the response selected by invocation/retry/normalization/acceptance behavior and contributes it to the current round response corpus.
Failed b contributes no evaluator output to subsequent round context.
Every b remains visible at the supervisory level regardless of success/failure.
Controller retains configured execution metadata for b.

requirements.instruction: Evaluate the configured supervisory failed-b stopping condition after a b reaches terminal state.
constraints: The condition uses visible terminal states of b batches.
A failed b may be recorded while processing continues when config permits.
When the failed-b stop condition is satisfied, use configured program failure return behavior.
Otherwise continue sequential b processing.

requirements.instruction: Advance sequentially through remaining b batches in the current B round.
constraints: Increment b only after the current b reaches terminal state and supervision permits continuation.
Process the next b only after the previous b completes.
Continue until all b batches terminate or supervisory failed-b logic stops the program.

requirements.instruction: Aggregate successful retained responses after all b batches in the current B round complete.
constraints: Only successful retained responses enter later reduction context.
Failed b remains visible in supervisory state but its output is excluded.
Call the token-counting function for retained responses when token counts are required.
round.aggregate_response_tokens is the sum of successful retained response token counts.
The retained response corpus remains serializable as next-round context.
Preserve provenance from retained responses to originating b batches.

requirements.instruction: Determine the post-round action after aggregation.
constraints: If terminal_round was already true before evaluating the current B round, completion of this round proceeds directly to configured program return.
A terminal B round performs no further termination check, division, or evaluator call.
If terminal_round was false, evaluate the configured termination condition against the completed round aggregate.
When that condition identifies the next B round as terminal, set terminal_round=true before advancing.
Setting the flag does not bypass the ordinary next-round division/evaluation path.

requirements.instruction: Advance a completed aggregate into the next B round when the program has not returned.
constraints: The successful retained aggregate becomes next-round context.
Increment B by exactly 1.
Return to B evaluation and resolve the complete iterator config for the new B.
Divide the new context and assign b batches before any evaluator invocation.

When terminal_round was set by the prior round, the configured termination/divider relationship is intended to produce one b; after that B round completes, return without another check/divide/evaluate cycle.

requirements.instruction: Preserve provenance throughout hierarchical reduction.
constraints: Each retained successful response remains traceable to its b.
Later results remain traceable through prior-round results toward source ancestry.
Later rounds may carry provenance identifiers instead of retransmitting full original source context.

requirements.instruction: Use one runtime token-counting function whenever the algorithm requires a token count.
constraints: Context assignment uses it for the one-time max_tokens assignment check.
Response measurement uses it when configured response conditions require tokens.
Round aggregation uses it for retained response token counts.
Retries do not cause another context-assignment token check.

requirements.instruction: Assemble and return the program result according to the configured program return envelope.
constraints: Return when the terminal B round completes or another configured program-level stopping condition terminates execution.
The configured envelope selects evaluator-produced and controller-produced values exposed by the runtime.
The exact program return envelope is configuration.

requirements.instruction: Provide B rules that resolve the complete configurable iterator behavior for each B round.
constraints: B rules are required.
Initial config defines B=0 and B>0 rules.
The intended initial B=0 rule resolves base evaluation behavior.
The intended initial B>0 rule resolves reduction/decision evaluation behavior.
A B rule may set or reference every setting defined as configurable on the iterator.

requirements.instruction: Represent evaluator behavior as configuration.
constraints: Evaluator config contains task, evaluation criteria, and response contract.
Additional supported evaluator settings may be configured.
Base/reduction/decision names are config references, not runtime classes.

requirements.instruction: Configure mechanical context division and maximum b context assignment.
constraints: divider.max_tokens is configurable and applies only to context assigned to b.
Evaluate max_tokens once per new b assignment.
The same assigned context persists through original invocation and retries.
Task, criteria, response contract, prior response, error data, and other invocation material are outside divider.max_tokens.
Boundary behavior is configurable.

requirements.instruction: Configure response-token conditions as values derived from divider.max_tokens.
constraints: Response thresholds use divider.max_tokens as reference.
The intended initial hard threshold is divider.max_tokens / 2.
Other thresholds may use configured divisors or ratios.
Preferred response size may be configured independently from hard response conditions.

requirements.instruction: Configure retry behavior as finite ordered conditionals.
constraints: Retry config defines conditions, ordered attempts, model inputs, success conditions, and terminal return behavior.
Different retries may receive different supported inputs.
The first successful retry is retained and later retries are skipped.

requirements.instruction: Provide the intended default system-error retry behavior.
constraints: Default: one fresh retry after the initial system failure.
The default retry repeats the original evaluator invocation as a fresh request.
If the fresh retry fails, record b failure and advance subject to supervisory failed-b stopping logic.
Config may replace this default.

requirements.instruction: Provide the intended default mechanically unacceptable-response retry behavior.
constraints: Default: one fresh corrective invocation.
It receives assigned original context, previous response, exact mechanical error, task, criteria, and response contract.
If corrective response succeeds, retain it.
If still mechanically unacceptable, default terminal behavior retains latest response with controller failure metadata and advances according to resulting b status.
Config may replace this default.

requirements.instruction: Configure mechanical response acceptance conditions.
constraints: Conditions inspect mechanically observable values.
Invocation state, required-response-field recovery, response-token conditions, and other supported mechanical conditions may be configured.
Resolved B iterator configuration determines applicable conditions for the round.

requirements.instruction: Configure the termination condition used to identify the terminal B round.
constraints: Termination is config, not a hard-coded algorithm expression.
The intended initial condition is round.aggregate_response_tokens / divider.max_tokens <= 1, equivalently aggregate_response_tokens <= divider.max_tokens.
Satisfying it sets terminal_round before the next B round.
The next B round follows normal B evaluation, division, b assignment, and evaluation; completion returns without another termination check/division.

requirements.instruction: Configure the supervisory stopping condition for failed b batches.
constraints: Config defines how many or what condition of failed b batches terminates the overall program.
A single failed b may permit continuation.
Every b remains visible at supervisory level.

requirements.instruction: Configure the program return envelope.
constraints: The envelope defines the returned structure when execution terminates.
It may select evaluator-produced and controller-produced values exposed by the runtime.
The controller assembles it.
The exact initial envelope will be supplied later.

requirements.instruction: Configure evaluator response contracts.
constraints: Each evaluator config identifies expected response structure.
Required fields are mechanically identifiable by the controller.
The contract is the basis for normalization and mechanical acceptance.
Exact downstream response contracts will be supplied later.
